title: the unsealed KEK goes to the box's own place, never a caller's TB_KEK_FILE (1457-6)

findings.claim: seal_keys.sh wrote the unsealed KEK where a caller's TB_KEK_FILE said (persistent disk with /etc/trialbox.kek) and D-887 then gave that folder to the services' user; fixed: the box's own /run/trialbox/kek always, the variable ignored with one line
tools.keys runtime_kek_path (unseal, escrow unseal, rotate-kek's runtime update) still falls back to the caller's TB_KEK_FILE when --out is not given; about 90 tests in 9 files use it as set-up

review of #1482, 1482-1: through the image (a host python3 without cryptography) the container was not given /run/trialbox-seal, so keys init --kek-in .../kek.new failed on every TPM seal and every re-run; fixed: the seal folder is mounted once arm has made it
review of #1482, 1482-2: no test pinned the folder check before the clean-up trap; with the traps first, a refused link's target kek.new would be shredded; fixed: a test that fails under that order
